Question 1

For the function f(x,y), calculate ∂2f∂x∂y given that ∂f∂y=−xyx2+y2.

a
 x2−y3(x2+y2)2
b
 y2(x−y)(x2+y2)2
c
 2x2−y2(x2+y2)2
d
 y(x2−y2)(x2+y2)2
e
y(x−y)x2+y2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To find ∂2f∂x∂y we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative ∂f∂y with respect to x:

∂2f∂x∂y=∂∂x(∂f∂y)=∂∂x(−xyx2+y2)=−y⋅∂∂x(xx2+y2)=−y(1x2+y2−2x2(x2+y2)2)=−y((x2+y2)−2x2(x2+y2)2)=y(x2−y2)(x2+y2)2

q-80396.name: Question 2
q-80396.problem: For the function $f(x,y),$ calculate $\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}}$ given that $\frac{∂f}{∂x}=2xy{e}^{({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})}.$
q-80396.worked_solution:
To find $\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}}$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative $\frac{∂f}{∂x}$ with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{∂f}{∂x}) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2xy{e}^{({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})}) \\  & =2y\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}(x{e}^{({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})}) \\  & =2y\cdot ({e}^{({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})}+2{x}^{2}{e}^{({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})}) \\  & =2y(1+2{x}^{2}){e}^{({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})}\end{aligned}
$$

q-132768.problem: For the function $f(x,y),$ calculate $\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y}$ given that $\frac{∂f}{∂y}=\frac{3{y}^{2}}{\sqrt{2x+{y}^{3}}}.$
q-132768.worked_solution:
To find $\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y}$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative $\frac{∂f}{∂y}$ with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{∂f}{∂y}) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{3{y}^{2}}{\sqrt{2x+{y}^{3}}}) \\  & =3{y}^{2}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}((2x+{y}^{3})^{-1/2}) \\  & =3{y}^{2}(-\frac{1}{2}\cdot (2x+{y}^{3})^{-3/2}\cdot 2) \\  & =-\frac{3{y}^{2}}{\sqrt{(2x+{y}^{3})^{3}}}\end{aligned}
$$

To find $\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y}$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative $\frac{∂f}{∂y}$ with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{∂f}{∂y}) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}y\operatorname{cos}⁡(x{y}^{2})) \\  & =y\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x{y}^{2})) \\  & =y\cdot (2x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x{y}^{2})-{x}^{2}{y}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x{y}^{2})) \\  & =2xy\operatorname{cos}⁡(x{y}^{2})-{x}^{2}{y}^{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x{y}^{2})\end{aligned}
$$

To find $\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y}$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative $\frac{∂f}{∂y}$ with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{∂f}{∂y}) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(-\frac{2{x}^{2}+y}{{y}^{3}}) \\  & =-\frac{1}{{y}^{3}}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}(2{x}^{2}+y) \\  & =-\frac{1}{{y}^{3}}(4x) \\  & =-\frac{4x}{{y}^{3}}\end{aligned}
$$

To find ${f}_{xx}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative ${f}_{x}(x,y)$ with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xx}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({f}_{x}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(-\frac{y}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}) \\  & =-y\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{1}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}) \\  & =-y\cdot (-\frac{2x}{({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})^{2}}) \\  & =\frac{2xy}{({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

To find ${f}_{yy}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative ${f}_{y}(x,y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{yy}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({f}_{y}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{x}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}) \\  & =x\cdot \frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{1}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}) \\  & =x\cdot (-\frac{2y}{({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})^{2}}) \\  & =-\frac{2xy}{({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xx}(x,y)+{f}_{yy}(x,y) & =\frac{2xy}{({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})^{2}}-\frac{2xy}{({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})^{2}}=0.\end{aligned}
$$

To find ${g}_{xy}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative ${g}_{x}(x,y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{xy}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({g}_{x}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(({x}^{2}+y){e}^{{y}^{2}}) \\  & ={e}^{{y}^{2}}+2y({x}^{2}+y){e}^{{y}^{2}} \\  & =(1+2{y}^{2}+2{x}^{2}y){e}^{{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

To find ${g}_{xx}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative ${g}_{x}(x,y)$ with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{xx}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({g}_{x}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(({x}^{2}+y){e}^{{y}^{2}}) \\  & =2x{e}^{{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{xy}(x,y)+{g}_{xx}(x,y) & =(1+2{y}^{2}+2{x}^{2}y){e}^{{y}^{2}}+2x{e}^{{y}^{2}} \\  & =(1+2x+2{y}^{2}+2{x}^{2}y){e}^{{y}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Find gxy(x,y)+gxx(x,y) given that gx(x,y)=(x2+y)ey2.

a
(1+x+x2y)ey2
b
(1+2x+y2)ey2

EXPLANATION

To find gxy(x,y) we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative gx(x,y) with respect to y:

gxy(x,y)=∂∂y(gx(x,y))=∂∂y((x2+y)ey2)=ey2+2y(x2+y)ey2=(1+2y2+2x2y)ey2

To find gxx(x,y) we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative gx(x,y) with respect to x:

gxx(x,y)=∂∂x(gx(x,y))=∂∂x((x2+y)ey2)=2xey2

Therefore, we have gxy(x,y)+gxx(x,y)=(1+2y2+2x2y)ey2+2xey2=(1+2x+2y2+2x2y)ey2.

q-132873.worked_solution:
To find ${f}_{xy}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative ${f}_{x}(x,y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xy}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({f}_{x}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(-\frac{{e}^{y}}{{x}^{2}}) \\  & =-\frac{{e}^{y}}{{x}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

To find ${f}_{yx}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative ${f}_{y}(x,y)$ with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{yx}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({f}_{y}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{{e}^{y}}{x}) \\  & =-\frac{{e}^{y}}{{x}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xy}(x,y)+{f}_{yx}(x,y) & =-\frac{{e}^{y}}{{x}^{2}}-\frac{{e}^{y}}{{x}^{2}}=-\frac{2{e}^{y}}{{x}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Find fxy(x,y)+fyx(x,y) given that fx(x,y)=−eyx2 and fy(x,y)=eyx.

a
−2eyx2
b
−2eyx3
c
−eyx
d
−ey(2+x)x2
e
−eyx2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To find fxy(x,y) we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative fx(x,y) with respect to y:

fxy(x,y)=∂∂y(fx(x,y))=∂∂y(−eyx2)=−eyx2

To find fyx(x,y) we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative fy(x,y) with respect to x:

fyx(x,y)=∂∂x(fy(x,y))=∂∂x(eyx)=−eyx2

Therefore, we have fxy(x,y)+fyx(x,y)=−eyx2−eyx2=−2eyx2.

q-80468.worked_solution:
To find ${f}_{xy}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative ${f}_{x}(x,y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xy}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({f}_{x}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(x\operatorname{cos}⁡({x}^{2}-{y}^{2})) \\  & =x\cdot (-\operatorname{sin}⁡({x}^{2}-{y}^{2})\cdot (-2y)) \\  & =2xy\operatorname{sin}⁡({x}^{2}-{y}^{2})\end{aligned}
$$

To find ${f}_{yx}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative ${f}_{y}(x,y)$ with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{yx}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({f}_{y}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(-y\operatorname{cos}⁡({x}^{2}-{y}^{2})) \\  & =-y(-\operatorname{sin}⁡({x}^{2}-{y}^{2})\cdot 2x) \\  & =2xy\operatorname{sin}⁡({x}^{2}-{y}^{2})\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xy}(x,y)+{f}_{yx}(x,y) & =2xy\operatorname{sin}⁡({x}^{2}-{y}^{2})+2xy\operatorname{sin}⁡({x}^{2}-{y}^{2}) \\  & =4xy\operatorname{sin}⁡({x}^{2}-{y}^{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

$$

Finally, we have

$$
{g}_{xx}(1,1)+{g}_{yy}(1,1)=e+e=2e.

q-80476.name: Question 11
q-80476.worked_solution:
First, we find the first-order derivative ${g}_{y}(x,y):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{y}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(x\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+y)) \\  & =\frac{x}{x+y}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find ${g}_{yy}(x,y)$ by differentiating ${g}_{y}(x,y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{yy}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({g}_{y}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{x}{x+y}) \\  & =-\frac{x}{(x+y)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we find ${g}_{yyx}(x,y)$ by differentiating ${g}_{yy}(x,y)$ with respect to $x:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{yyx}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({g}_{yy}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(-\frac{x}{(x+y)^{2}}) \\  & =-\frac{1}{(x+y)^{2}}+\frac{2x}{(x+y)^{3}} \\  & =\frac{-(x+y)+2x}{(x+y)^{3}} \\  & =\frac{x-y}{(x+y)^{3}}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(y+z)) \\  & =2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(y+z)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find ${f}_{xy}(x,y,z)$ by differentiating ${f}_{x}(x,y,z)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xy}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({f}_{x}(x,y,z)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(y+z)) \\  & =2x\cdot \frac{1}{y+z} \\  & =\frac{2x}{y+z}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find ${f}_{xyz}(x,y,z)$ by differentiating ${f}_{xy}(x,y,z)$ with respect to $z:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xyz}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂z}({f}_{xy}(x,y,z)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂z}(\frac{2x}{y+z}) \\  & =2x\cdot \frac{∂}{∂z}(\frac{1}{y+z}) \\  & =2x\cdot (-\frac{1}{(y+z)^{2}}) \\  & =-\frac{2x}{(y+z)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate ${f}_{xyz}(x,y,z)$ at $(-5,2,3):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xyz}(-5,2,3) & =-\frac{2(-5)}{(2+3)^{2}}=\frac{2}{5}\end{aligned}

fxyx(x,y)=∂∂x(fxy(x,y))=∂∂x(4xy+ex)=4⋅1⋅y+ex=4y+ex
